title: James Butler, 1st Duke of Ormond, to his son the Earl of Arran, 24 January 1677/8: twenty code figures set as 'a trial whether you are skilful in deciphering' (HMC Ormonde n.s. iv p. 93; Unsolved Catalogue 353)

steps.what: IA full text of HMC Ormonde n.s. iv-v fetched and searched; the passage is the only run of cipher figures in vol. iv; no gloss printed.
p. 93 scan checked: 20 figures; the sixth of run 1 is 58, correcting the 57 in Tomokiyo's quotation and the catalogue.
Ormond-Arran code of 1678 (Arran to Ormond 9 Feb 1677/8, HMC n.s. iv pp. 105-106, with Ormond's interlinear equivalents) examined: a two-letter code (hm, dk, io, yn.xo...), not numeric.

Ormond-Longford 1680 key structure (Tomokiyo's reconstruction from HMC n.s. v pp. 454 ff.; letter slots checked on vol. v p. 498) applied: the low figures 32 33 54 55 58 fall on k l h i m and give consonant runs between alphabetical neighbours, no English. Agrees with Tomokiyo's rejected trial.

Manuscript sought: NLI Sources MS UR 006261 (Ormond to Arran, Jan 7, 24 ... 1678, Ormonde MSS); NLI list A017 puts the 1665-80 letters in MSS 2335-2362. Volume and folio not identified; not digitised.
20 figures, 20 distinct, range 32-732: no repeats to anchor a ciphertext-only solver; no solver run, since a same-length control in a code of this size cannot succeed.

Tomokiyo's Ormond-Longford Cipher 1 (1680) applied with every 1678 figure reduced by 7: run 2 reads 'to Ormond not c-re-di-b-le', run 1 'an-d King ar-e in a'. Offsets -150..+150 on Longford 1 and 2 (602 trials) and Longford 3.

Every 1680 value used checked on the page images of HMC n.s. V pp.454, 469, 479, 486, 498 (identification/GLOSS_CHECK.md); 566 = Ormond rests on the plain rendering on p.498 and the gloss 'Dor' on p.454; 418 = King is context only.

Longest vocabulary word over 3+ groups: only -7 of 301 offsets on K1 gives one ('credible'); 2,000 random figure sets at their best of 602 key-offset pairs reach 8+ letters 6/2000; 3,000 shuffles at -7 reach 8+ letters 0/3000 (identification/controls_out.txt).

Integration check of PR #526: decode.py, controls.py and controls_joint.py re-run (python3 -I): every figure reproduced (14/20 at -7 on Tomokiyo's key; only -7 of 602 key-offset trials spells a 5+ letter word, 'credible'; random sets 8+ letters 6/2000; hit count 14 in 5/2000; shuffles 0/3000). Own decoder from Tomokiyo's table image: same 14 values. Own control with another lexicon (lang/lexicons/en.json.gz, words of 6+ letters): only -7 spells one; random sets 8+ letters 0/1000. p.93 figures 20/20 on the scan; glosses checked on pp.454, 469, 479, 486, 498: on p.486 'and' stands over 84 alone and 'i' over 50, so 84 = 'an' is the contributor's reading. Strict share 10/20 = 50% (interpolated and context values are holes); class read in part.

texts.label: Ormond to Arran, 24 January 1677/8 (HMC n.s. iv p. 93)
texts.summary: Ormond, Lord Lieutenant at Dublin, writes to his son Arran in London about William Douglas, a Scottish preacher whose tale of a covenanting rising had come to nothing. Two names and a clause are in figures, set as a trial of Arran's skill in deciphering; the figures say that if Douglas is right someone and the King are in some danger or plot, 'but it seems to Ormond not credible'.

reading_review.note: The second run reads as a clause that completes the clear words ('but it seems to Ormond not credible'); the first run reads only around its holes ('[726] and King are in a [700] [720]', with King from context). 10 of 20 figures attested.

prior.where: none found: Cryptiana charlesii2.htm lists the passage as unidentified and its hidden trial at offset 0 was rejected; Tomokiyo's 1680 key itself is published. The offset is new by the contributor's record (identification/PRIOR_ART.md).

human: Malcolm McBratney ran an agent on Perplexity that noticed the offset; he set the check task. No other input.
